cells.tense: You are open to feeling before there is anything in particular to feel.
cells.ask: Name one thing you noticed today that you'd normally let pass unregistered — just name it to yourself. Then get on with your day, keeping it.
cells.core:
You're open to something that hasn't arrived yet. Not waiting for a name — the readiness itself, the heart before it has anything to carry. And you're willing for it to stay nameless a little longer; that's what lets you actually take it in.

The thing that would set you up next is letting yourself go toward one of those open possibilities. You know how to hold a window open. What's left is turning toward whichever feeling is most alive in you, before you decide whether to keep it. That's where more gets in. Allure — pulled by what might be felt, not by what you'll do with it once it comes.
cells.sheetLine: You're open before you know what you're opening to.
cells.verb: opening to the first trace of what will be felt
cells.place: the seed state where everything is possible because nothing has been chosen yet

cells.tense: You'll be open to everything by tomorrow, and you're already at the edge of what you can hold.
cells.ask: When the next pull comes, wait a full minute before you respond to it — just watch it, and let the minute end before anything else.
cells.core:
You're bracing for an opening that hasn't finished arriving. There's still a picture of yourself carrying every feeling in the room and carrying it perfectly, and you're already living in that picture — so every possible thing gets marked as yours to feel, and none of it lands. The waiting for it is getting in the way of having it.

When the next pull shows up, don't follow it on reflex. Let it hang there for a minute. You've been enjoying the feeling of being about to receive more than the receiving, and a pause is the one place that gets reversed. Achievement — completion of the form you actually picked, rather than the one you were gathering yourself to be ready for.
cells.sheetLine: You gather feelings that haven't arrived, and they don't land.

cells.tense: You stood at that opening before, and your feet are still pointed the other way.
cells.ask: Pick one person or thing and be available to it without knowing what you'll get back. Say out loud what you notice, even a small thing.
cells.core:
The openness worked before, and it stopped. Opening to feeling is not something you do now, so staying ready stopped seeming worth it, and you've been living on the far side of that ever since. The vessel is still there. It just hasn't been turned toward anything new.

What you're open to is still real, even if you haven't felt it lately. Being ready is present; it's the approach to the present moment that isn't, because you stepped back before the moment had a chance to arrive. Realization — carrying what the last opening became. One thing you notice in front of you today is enough to start. Not a feeling. A fact.
cells.sheetLine: You're open to nothing because you're holding a door open that already shut.

cells.tense: You are already receiving, and you keep calling it being sensible about what you take.
cells.ask: Find the last thing you received — time, help, attention — and tell the person who gave it what it gave you.
cells.core:
You're already open to something and you keep describing it as just being realistic. The receiving is happening — you're moved by things, you take people in, you let small things land — and you narrate it as if you were simply being sensible about what to take in.

Meanwhile you give in the same motion without tracking that either. Reciprocity — the plain act of receiving and passing back, done between two people while it's still warm. The openness is functioning, and its author keeps declining the credit. One exchange, said out loud, and you'd be able to tell what was yours to begin with.
cells.sheetLine: You're already open. You're calling it not taking much.
